_comment: Model-authored interpretation (Claude Code, Step 2 v1). Numbers are NEVER typed here: every {placeholder} is filled by src/build_diagnosis.py from output/step1 and config/account_context.json; an unknown placeholder or term_id fails the build. Human amendments belong in a separate file, not here.
author: claude-code-model-interpretation

status_legend.fact: taken from supplied data or confirmed context
status_legend.to_confirm: needs product/data/operator input before it can become a decision

st_dd3412fed286.evidence_summary: Largest term: {cost_share_pct} of sample spend and {sub_share_pct} of sample subs. Cost/sub {cost_per_sub} is {ratio_to_allowable} of the $181 allowable and {ratio_to_benchmark} of the scope benchmark ({benchmark}). Signup rate {signup_per_click_pct}, signup->sub {paid_sub_per_signup_pct}. Phrase match on the core category term.

intent_hypothesis.text: Core category intent: user wants a tool that builds AI apps. Closest match to the scope label itself.

missing_info.item: existing keyword and match type this term is served by
missing_info.limits: whether it is already the head keyword or a broad-match spillover; bid/isolation decisions
whether there is headroom to scale on this term at all
whether {paid_sub} subs are mature for the same-period {signup} signups

st_dd3412fed286.under_scale: Primary expansion candidate: below allowable with the most volume. Confirm headroom (impression share) before raising bids or budget; adding spend without headroom would not add subs.
st_dd3412fed286.under_maintain_efficiency: Keep as is. It anchors the sample below the benchmark; no change unless a cohort-aligned cost/sub comes in above $181.
investigate_now: Pull impression share and top-of-page rate for the matching keyword(s).
Confirm which keyword/ad group serves this phrase-match term.

st_7397eeb3716a.evidence_summary: Second-largest spend ({cost_share_pct} of sample). Highest signup count in the sample ({signup}, {signup_per_click_pct} of clicks) and cheapest signups ({cost_per_signup}), but signup->sub is {paid_sub_per_signup_pct}, so cost/sub is {cost_per_sub}: {ratio_to_allowable} of allowable and {ratio_to_benchmark} of the benchmark. Removing it arithmetically leaves the rest of the sample at {sample_without_term_cost_per_sub}/sub (arithmetic, not a forecast).

intent_hypothesis.text: Price-sensitive or exploratory intent: wants to try without paying. Whether that is on-path depends entirely on whether Braid has a free tier and how long free->paid takes.

missing_info.item: does Braid have a free tier, and what is the free->paid conversion window
missing_info.limits: whether the {paid_sub} subs are immature (lag) or the intent is genuinely low-value; the whole negative-vs-keep decision

missing_info.item: FFT or activation events for these signups
missing_info.limits: whether the {signup} signups show product usage or are dead accounts
whether the 'free' promise on the SERP is matched or contradicted post-click

st_7397eeb3716a.under_scale: Do not scale on cost/sub; the signup volume is attractive only if a bidding signal (FFT/activation) confirms these signups progress. Candidate to isolate into its own ad group with a free-tier landing page and a lower bid so it stops sharing budget with the core term.
st_7397eeb3716a.under_maintain_efficiency: Conditional negative on 'free' (phrase) if the product has no free tier or the free cohort does not convert after the lag window. If a free tier exists, isolate and cap rather than negate: this term produces the most signups in the sample.
investigate_now: Ask product: free tier yes/no, and the median days from free signup to paid.
Pull cohort-aligned subs for these signups (60/90-day) instead of same-window subs.
Check the landing page for this term against the 'free' promise.

st_2fe617db21cf.search_term: how to build an ai app
st_2fe617db21cf.evidence_summary: {cost_share_pct} of sample spend, cost/sub {cost_per_sub}: {ratio_to_allowable} of allowable and {ratio_to_benchmark} of the benchmark. Cheap clicks ({cpc}) and a {signup_per_click_pct} signup rate, but signup->sub only {paid_sub_per_signup_pct}.

intent_hypothesis.text: Informational / learning intent; a share of searchers are looking for a tutorial rather than a product. Broad match may also be pulling adjacent 'how to' queries not visible here.

missing_info.item: the actual queries grouped under this broad-match term and the matched keyword
missing_info.limits: whether this is one intent or a mixed bucket; negative scoping
whether a tutorial/template page could lift signup->sub
informational visitors may convert later; same-window subs may understate

st_2fe617db21cf.under_scale: Not a scaling candidate at {cost_per_sub}. Test a how-to/template landing page first; if signup->sub moves toward the sample average, revisit.
st_2fe617db21cf.under_maintain_efficiency: Bid down or move to a separate ad group with its own budget. A 'how to' phrase negative in the core ad group is conditional on confirming the queries are mostly tutorial-seeking.
investigate_now: Export the search-term report for the matching keyword to see the query mix.
Run a landing-page test: template/tutorial page vs current page, measured on signup->sub.

st_98934dc150fb.evidence_summary: Cost/sub {cost_per_sub} ({ratio_to_allowable} of allowable, {ratio_to_benchmark} of benchmark) with the second-highest sub count ({paid_sub}, {sub_share_pct} of sample subs). Signup->sub {paid_sub_per_signup_pct} is above the sample's larger terms.

intent_hypothesis.text: No-code builder intent. Efficient here, but whether Braid positions itself as no-code is unknown; if not, this may be an adjacent audience converting on a different promise.

missing_info.item: no-code positioning and whether a no-code keyword/ad group already exists
missing_info.limits: add vs already-covered; landing-page choice
scaling headroom

st_98934dc150fb.under_scale: Expansion candidate: check existing coverage, then consider a dedicated no-code ad group and landing page to protect the {paid_sub_per_signup_pct} signup->sub rate while adding volume.
st_98934dc150fb.under_maintain_efficiency: Keep; consider isolating so its efficiency is not diluted by broad-match neighbours.
investigate_now: Check the existing keyword list for 'no code' / 'without code' variants before adding anything.
Confirm product positioning on no-code with product/marketing.

st_a3029027e1c6.evidence_summary: Cost/sub {cost_per_sub}: {ratio_to_allowable} of allowable (below it) but {ratio_to_benchmark} of the benchmark (close to it). {cost_share_pct} of sample spend, signup->sub {paid_sub_per_signup_pct}.

intent_hypothesis.text: Trend-driven intent ('vibe coding') for an AI-assisted builder. Likely aligned with the product category, but the phrase is new and its searcher mix may shift quickly.

missing_info.item: whether Braid's messaging uses or fits 'vibe coding'
missing_info.limits: landing-page/ad-copy alignment
whether to invest in a dedicated keyword

st_a3029027e1c6.under_scale: Secondary expansion candidate, below allowable. Isolate with matching ad copy before adding budget so that efficiency can be observed separately.
st_a3029027e1c6.under_maintain_efficiency: Hold. It is within allowable; monitor since it sits near the benchmark.
investigate_now: Check existing keyword coverage for 'vibe coding'.

st_6de9a251f911.evidence_summary: Highest cost/sub in the sample: {cost_per_sub}, {ratio_to_allowable} of allowable. Most expensive clicks ({cpc}) and signups ({cost_per_signup}); only {paid_sub} subs from {signup} signups ({paid_sub_per_signup_pct}). {cost_share_pct} of sample spend. Small counts: no operator data-sufficiency threshold has been set, so 'low data' is a judgement, not a rule.

intent_hypothesis.text: Enterprise buyer / evaluator intent. If Braid sells to enterprises via sales, these visitors would appear as leads, not self-serve subs, and cost/sub would not be the right KPI for this term. If Braid has no enterprise motion, the term is off-target.

missing_info.item: enterprise offering and sales-assisted path (demo requests, SQLs)
missing_info.limits: the entire keep/negative decision; whether Subs is even the right KPI
whether {paid_sub} subs is enough evidence to act on
whether the high CPC is avoidable

st_6de9a251f911.under_scale: Not scaled on cost/sub. If an enterprise motion exists, route to a demo/contact landing page and judge on leads; otherwise exclude.
st_6de9a251f911.under_maintain_efficiency: Conditional negative on 'enterprise' (phrase) if there is no enterprise offering or sales path. If there is one, move the term to a separate ad group with enterprise-specific measurement instead of negating.
investigate_now: Ask sales/product: is there an enterprise plan or sales-assisted path, and are demo requests tracked?
Check whether any of these {signup} signups became sales leads.

st_a9cf56135541.evidence_summary: Second-lowest cost/sub in the sample: {cost_per_sub} ({ratio_to_allowable} of allowable). Second-highest signup->sub in the sample ({paid_sub_per_signup_pct}) and {paid_sub} subs on {cost_share_pct} of spend.

intent_hypothesis.text: Use-case intent: build internal business tools. Converts well, which suggests the product serves this use case, but that is inferred from the data, not confirmed by product.

missing_info.item: whether internal tools is a supported/promoted use case
missing_info.limits: landing-page and ad-copy investment
add vs already covered

st_a9cf56135541.under_scale: Expansion candidate: confirm coverage, then dedicated ad group + use-case landing page.
investigate_now: Check keyword list and landing pages for an internal-tools use case.
Confirm with product whether internal tools is a target use case.

st_429e31f7f0f8.evidence_summary: Cost/sub {cost_per_sub}: {ratio_to_allowable} of allowable. Cheapest clicks in the sample ({cpc}) and a normal signup rate ({signup_per_click_pct}), but signup->sub is only {paid_sub_per_signup_pct} ({paid_sub} subs from {signup} signups). {cost_share_pct} of sample spend.

intent_hypothesis.text: Developer intent: looking for an open-source repo, a GitHub-integrated builder, or code export. If Braid has no GitHub integration or does not target developers, this is off-target; if it does, the landing page may be failing this audience.

missing_info.item: GitHub integration / code export / developer targeting
missing_info.limits: negative vs landing-page fix

missing_info.item: landing page shown to this query
missing_info.limits: whether developers see anything GitHub-related

st_429e31f7f0f8.under_scale: Not scaled. If developers are a target, test a developer/GitHub landing page before deciding.
st_429e31f7f0f8.under_maintain_efficiency: Conditional negative on 'github' (phrase) if there is no GitHub-related feature or developer targeting. If there is, fix the landing page first and re-measure.
investigate_now: Ask product: GitHub integration or code export, yes/no.
Check what the ad and landing page promise for this query.

st_66770c31f114.evidence_summary: Lowest cost/sub in the sample: {cost_per_sub} ({ratio_to_allowable} of allowable, {ratio_to_benchmark} of benchmark). Highest signup rate ({signup_per_click_pct}) and highest signup->sub ({paid_sub_per_signup_pct}). Small spend ({cost_share_pct} of sample) at a {cpc} CPC.

intent_hypothesis.text: Competitor-switching intent: Scaffold is the confirmed main competitor, so these are evaluators comparing alternatives. High readiness to buy is consistent with the ratios.

missing_info.limits: whether this is already targeted or is broad-match spillover
scaling headroom

missing_info.item: trademark/policy constraints on competitor ad copy
missing_info.limits: ad copy for a dedicated ad group

st_66770c31f114.under_scale: Clear expansion candidate: check coverage, then a dedicated competitor ad group with a comparison landing page and its own budget.
st_66770c31f114.under_maintain_efficiency: Keep and isolate; still worth a dedicated ad group so the efficient volume is protected.
investigate_now: Check whether a competitor campaign or 'scaffold' keywords already exist.
Pull impression share for competitor queries.

negative_candidates.condition: only if product confirms no free tier OR cohort-aligned free->paid conversion stays near the same-window rate after the lag window; otherwise isolate, do not negate
only if product confirms no GitHub integration/code export and developers are not a target; otherwise fix landing page first
only if there is no enterprise offering or sales-assisted path; if there is, Subs is the wrong KPI and the term should be measured on leads instead
negative_candidates.scope_note: campaign/ad-group IDs unknown; small counts, no data-sufficiency threshold set

negative_candidates.condition: only under maintain_efficiency and only after the query mix confirms mostly tutorial-seeking; a landing-page test is the preferred first step
negative_candidates.scope_note: would apply to the core ad group only; IDs unknown

addition_or_isolation_candidates.action: isolate into a competitor ad group
isolate into a use-case ad group
addition_or_isolation_candidates.precheck: existing keyword coverage; product confirms use case

addition_or_isolation_candidates.action: isolate into a no-code ad group
isolate with free-tier landing page and capped bid (if free tier exists)
addition_or_isolation_candidates.landing_page_test: free-tier page vs current, measured on cohort-aligned subs

addition_or_isolation_candidates.action: separate ad group for informational queries

least_certain_term.why: It is {cost_share_pct} of sample spend, produces the most signups, and its decision flips entirely on one product fact. Every other high cost/sub term has a smaller spend footprint.
least_certain_term.single_piece_of_information: Whether Braid has a free tier and, if so, the cohort-aligned free->paid conversion after the lag window. If free signups convert later at a rate that brings cost/sub under $181, the term is an isolation candidate; if not, it is the largest negative candidate.

questions_for_product_or_data_team.question: Is there a free tier? What is the median and 90-day free->paid conversion?
Is there a GitHub integration, code export, or developer audience?
Is there an enterprise plan or sales-assisted path, and are demo requests tracked as conversions?
questions_for_product_or_data_team.unblocks: enterprise app development platform decision and KPI choice

questions_for_product_or_data_team.question: Are no-code, internal tools and vibe coding positioning the product supports?
questions_for_product_or_data_team.unblocks: isolation and landing-page choices for three efficient terms

questions_for_product_or_data_team.question: What are the exact dates, attribution model, and lag between Regs and Subs? Are Subs cohort-aligned to Regs in the same window?
questions_for_product_or_data_team.unblocks: whether signup->sub ratios are comparable across terms

questions_for_product_or_data_team.question: Is there an FFT/activation event available per search term?
Customer value or margin behind the $181 allowable, and whether it differs by plan?
questions_for_product_or_data_team.unblocks: whether $181 is right for enterprise or free-tier intents

questions_for_product_or_data_team.question: Existing keyword list, match types, campaign/ad-group structure and IDs; impression share by keyword
questions_for_product_or_data_team.unblocks: add-vs-covered decisions, negative scoping, and any Editor file

other_hypotheses_and_tests.hypothesis: The sample cost/sub ({sample_cost_per_sub}) is above the scope benchmark ({benchmark}); by subtraction the unseen ~35% of scope spend runs at {remainder_cost_per_sub}. The nine rows may be the harder part of the scope, not representative of it.
other_hypotheses_and_tests.test: Request the full search-term report for the scope.

other_hypotheses_and_tests.hypothesis: Three low-converting terms (free / github / enterprise) share a pattern: normal or high signup rate, very low signup->sub. That is consistent with either intent mismatch or post-click mismatch; the data cannot separate the two.
other_hypotheses_and_tests.test: Landing-page audit per term before any negative.

other_hypotheses_and_tests.hypothesis: Broad match may be grouping several intents under one row (e.g. 'how to build an ai app').
Non-Brand Q2 cost/sub ({non_brand_cost_per_sub}) rose versus supplied Q1 ({non_brand_q1_cost_per_sub}); the scope's contribution to that change cannot be isolated without period alignment.
other_hypotheses_and_tests.test: Confirm the scope period equals Q2 and get Q1 scope figures.

channel_context_observations: Google Non-Brand is the largest channel ({non_brand_spend_share} of paid spend) at {non_brand_cost_per_sub}/sub, below its $181 allowable, and up from supplied Q1 {non_brand_q1_cost_per_sub}. Q1 cannot be recomputed.

Google Performance Max ({pmax_cost_per_sub}/sub vs $181 allowable) and Meta prospecting ({meta_prospecting_cost_per_sub}/sub vs $142) are the channels above allowable. Reddit is slightly above ($158). These are descriptive comparisons; causes are not established here.
Paid total supplied cost/sub ({paid_total_supplied}) differs from the recomputed {paid_total_recomputed}; cause unknown, both retained.
TikTok has no allowable; no gap is computed.
